cards.name: Airbnb listing (title and description)
cards.summary: A listing's title and description on Airbnb. Airbnb asks for a title of fewer than 50 characters because longer ones are shortened in search, starting with the most important information, in sentence case, with no emojis or repeated symbols. No source read caps the description; Airbnb asks for a brief, specific, realistic description that tells the story of the space.
use_for: Title for a homestay, villa, apartment or room: type of space + place or landmark + one thing that sets it apart.
The opening of the description: what the space is and who it suits, before any list.
Rewriting a listing that gets views but few bookings.
Honest 'good to know' lines about stairs, children, pets and mobility.
Experience and service titles (these are reviewed before they go live).
avoid: Title in ALL CAPS, with emojis or with '!!!' / '***'. Airbnb capitalises only the first word plus proper names and abbreviations, bars emojis and symbols in titles (Content Policy), and allows single special characters but not repeated ones. Separate ideas with commas or one slash.
A title that saves the best fact for the end. Longer titles are shortened in search, so the tail is what disappears. Put the most important information first.
A description that repeats the amenities list. Airbnb says lead with what matters and be specific ('a perfect base for exploring the city'); the amenities already have their own section.
Hiding stairs, no lift, children or mobility limits. Airbnb asks hosts to be upfront about challenges, and misleading information breaches the Content Policy.
Quoting a 500-character description cap or a 32-character visible title from memory. Both circulate on third-party sites only and were not found on Airbnb's own pages.

sources.title: Guidelines for writing your listing title - Airbnb Resource Center
sources.supports: title length, sentence case, no emojis or repeated symbols

sources.title: Edit your listing's title - Airbnb Help Center
sources.supports: no symbols or emojis in titles (Content Policy); title changes take up to an hour; service/experience titles need review

sources.title: Writing an effective listing description - Airbnb Resource Center (updated Nov 28, 2023)
sources.supports: description guidance: brief, specific, story of the space, realistic

limits.field: listing title (recommended; longer titles are shortened in search)
limits.quote: Start with the most important information, and try to use fewer than 50 characters. Longer titles are automatically shortened in search results
limits.confidence: high (official Airbnb Resource Center, dated Feb 2, 2026)

formatting: Title: plain text in sentence case. Capitalise only the first word plus proper names and abbreviations (neighbourhood, landmark, airport code).
No emojis or symbols in titles (Content Policy). A single special character is fine; do not repeat one for emphasis (!!!, ***). Separate ideas with commas or a single slash.
Airbnb shortens longer titles automatically in search results to fit smaller screens, so the end of a long title may not show.
Title changes take up to an hour to appear; service and experience titles need review before they publish (Airbnb Help Center).

Description: no official length cap was found (the 500-character figure is third-party only: unverified). Bold, lists and line breaks are not covered by the pages read: unverified; write short plain-text paragraphs and check the host editor.
Hindi or Hinglish text in a title is not addressed by the sources: unverified; keep titles in the language guests search in.
writing_notes: Lint: this card has one lintable limit, so `pcw.py check title.txt --platform plat:airbnb_listing` tests the TITLE against 50 characters, no --field needed. Paste only the title. The description has no recorded cap, so the lint does not test its length; judge it by reading.
Airbnb words the 50 as 'try to use fewer than 50 characters' and says longer titles are shortened in search. Treat 50 as a hard ceiling for writing: anything past it is the part guests will not see.

Title formula: type of space + place or landmark + one differentiator, in sentence case. Examples: 'Sea-view 2BHK, 5 minutes from Palolem Beach' (43 chars) and 'Courtyard room in a Jaipur haveli, near Hawa Mahal' (50 chars). Wrong: 'BEST LUXURY VILLA!!! 🌴 Goa Stay' (capitals, repeated symbols, emoji, and no fact a guest can use).

Description order: line 1, the space and who it suits; 2-3 short sentences of specific story (what the morning looks like, what is a short walk away); then the honest limits (stairs, noise, shared areas); house rules last. Do not paste the amenities list again.

Example 'good to know' line: 'The flat is on the second floor and the building has no lift, so it may not suit guests who find stairs difficult.' Say it plainly; guests who arrive knowing book happier.
Write specific, checkable facts (walking minutes you have timed, floor, bed sizes). Airbnb asks for realistic descriptions, so do not use 'luxury' or 'best' without something that shows it.

algorithm_notes.note: Airbnb: longer titles are automatically shortened in search results to fit smaller screens, so the first words of a title do the work.

cards.name: Amazon Brand Store (Stores builder pages and tiles)
cards.summary: A Brand Store is a free multi-page storefront built from tiles. The one number Amazon prints for its text is a recommendation: keep header copy under 30 characters so it can be set large enough to read on mobile. Amazon publishes no caps for text-tile or image-with-text fields; the builder enforces its own.
use_for: Header copy on the Store's pages (a short noun-phrase promise).
Text tile for brand history and mission.
Image-with-text tile: prefix, heading, body and link text over or beside an image.
Rewriting a Store so the words survive on a phone.
avoid: Baking the headline into the image. Amazon says text in an image 'will not be readable by search engines, or by people who rely on screen readers'; use the Image with text tile so the words stay real text.

A header longer than 30 characters. Amazon's mobile guide asks for under 30 so the type can be big (it also recommends a minimum 90 pt Arial-equivalent font for header copy); a long header forces small type.
Putting the one essential line in a field that only shows on desktop. Some text fields are not supported in the custom mobile layout; keep the key message in tiles that show on mobile.
Quoting tile character limits from memory. The Stores spec page publishes none; read the builder's live counter.
Link text such as 'Click here' on a tile: say the destination ('Shop the masala blends').

sources.title: Stores creative guidelines - Ad specs & Requirements | Amazon Ads
sources.supports: tile types (text, image with text: prefix, heading, body, link text), image sizes, embedded-text guidance, desktop-only text fields

sources.title: Six tips to optimize your Brand Store for mobile | Amazon Ads
sources.supports: header copy length and font-size advice

sources.title: A comprehensive guide to successful Brand Stores | Amazon Ads
sources.supports: text tiles for brand history and mission, byline traffic, logo 400 x 400 px minimum

limits.quote: The copy in the header should be less than 30 characters ... to be legible on mobile
limits.confidence: medium (official Amazon Ads guide; a recommendation, not a field cap)

formatting: Tile types that carry words: Text tile (freeform text that can link to a Store page or product detail page) and Image with text tile.
Image with text, text over image: prefix, heading, body and link text. Text next to image: header and description.
Header copy: under 30 characters (recommendation); the mobile guide also recommends a minimum 90 pt Arial-equivalent font for header copy.
Text in the image itself is discouraged: search engines and screen readers cannot read it.
Some text fields do not appear in the custom mobile layout and show on desktop only.
Logo: 400 x 400 px minimum (Stores best-practices guide).
Bold, line breaks, emoji and Hindi text inside tiles are not covered by the pages read: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: one lintable limit, so `pcw.py check header.txt --platform plat:amazon_brand_store` tests the header copy against 30 characters. Paste only the header. The other tile fields have no recorded cap, so the lint cannot test them; use the builder's counter.

Header formula: a noun-phrase promise, not a greeting. 'Small-batch chai from Pune' (26 chars) or 'Chai, blended in Pune' (21 chars). Wrong: 'Welcome to the Official Brew Rani Store' (39 chars, and it says nothing a shopper can use).

Text tile: brand history and mission (Amazon's best-practices use for it) in 2-4 short sentences, one idea each, ending on what the shopper can do next. Example: 'Brew Rani began with one family recipe for masala chai in Pune. Today we blend small batches of Assam tea with whole cardamom and dry ginger and pack them ourselves.'

Image-with-text tile: prefix as a short label, heading as the product or collection, body as one line of specs, link text as verb + destination. Example: prefix 'New blend', heading 'Cardamom Kadak', body 'Assam tea, whole cardamom, dry ginger.', link text 'Shop the blend'.
Write for the phone first: if the line does not fit large on a narrow screen, cut words, do not shrink the font.
Every product claim on a tile must match the product detail page; if the pack does not show it, do not say it.

algorithm_notes.note: Amazon Stores spec: text baked into an image will not be readable by search engines or by people who rely on screen readers, so use the Image with text tile.

cards.name: Amazon DSP display creatives (responsive eCommerce, asset-based, Brand Store creative)
cards.summary: Amazon DSP display creatives are built from fields with hard caps. Responsive eCommerce creative: headline 50 characters, disclaimer 60 characters, at most 10 words on a custom image. Asset-based and Brand Store creative: headline 50, brand name 25, body text 100, up to 15 headlines and 5 body texts per asset-based creative. The headline rules matter as much as the numbers: no price or savings claims, no exclamation points, no unsupported superlatives.
use_for: Headline for a responsive eCommerce creative built from a product image.
Words for a size-specific custom image (10 words at most).
A set of up to 15 headlines and 5 body texts for an asset-based creative, plus brand name.
The optional disclaimer line for products that need one.
avoid: Pricing or savings in the headline ('Rs 99', 'Flat 30% off'). Amazon bars them there. Describe the product or the benefit and let the product data carry the price.
Forceful phrases and exclamation points ('Don't miss out!') or several punctuation marks or special characters in a row. Write one plain sentence fragment.
'Best', 'top selling', 'healthiest' and similar claims Amazon will not accept without support. Use a fact that is true and checkable on the product (ingredient, weight, place packed).
Subscribe & Save messaging in any headline.
More than 10 words on a custom image, Title Case on it, or more than 2 type variations. Image copy is sentence case.
Fifteen headlines that are one line reworded fifteen ways. Give each a different angle (ingredient, occasion, place made, gifting) so the set is worth having.
Assuming the Japan counts (25 headline, 15 brand, 50 body) apply to India. Amazon prints them for Japan; how Devanagari is counted is not stated, so check the console counter for Hindi.

sources.title: eCommerce display creatives - Guidelines & ad specs | Amazon Ads
sources.supports: headline/disclaimer limits and headline rules, custom image word cap, sentence case for image copy

sources.title: Asset-based and Brand Store Creatives - Guidelines & ad spec | Amazon Ads
sources.supports: per-field limits and component counts (Brand Store creative 1 of each; asset-based up to 15 headlines, 5 body texts)

limits.quote: Maximum of 50 characters in the headline.
Maximum of 60 Characters in the disclaimer.

limits.field: words on a size-specific custom image
limits.quote: Total words in the custom image may not exceed 10 words (40 characters in JP).
Headline 50 characters ; 25 JP characters
Brand Name 25 characters ; 15 JP characters
Body Text 100 characters ; 50 JP characters
Headline 50 characters ; 25 JP characters 1 15 (columns: Brand store Creative / Asset based Creative components per field)

formatting: Headline: plain text starting with a capital letter (except certain brand names); no multiple punctuation marks or special characters in a row.
Copy inside custom images: sentence case, at most 2 type variations, at most 10 words.
Disclaimer: only for products that need one; 60 characters in responsive eCommerce creative.
CTA: picked from a pre-approved dropdown, not written by the copywriter.
Component counts: Brand Store creative takes 1 of each field; asset-based creative takes up to 15 headlines and 5 body texts.
Japan limits are roughly half (25 JP characters for the headline, 15 for brand name, 50 for body).
Emoji, line breaks and Hindi are not covered by the specs read: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: six lintable fields, so always pass --field. `--field "headline (responsive"` (50 chars, eCommerce creative), `--field "headline (asset-based"` (50 chars), `--field disclaimer` (60), `--field "words on a size-specific"` (10 words), `--field "brand name"` (25), `--field "body text"` (100). Both headline caps are 50; choose the --field that names the ad type you are writing.
The 15-headlines-per-creative limit is a count the tool cannot test: count them by hand. Check one headline per run, because the lint measures the whole file.

Headline formula: product + one checkable benefit, no price, no verb of urgency. 'Whole-spice masala chai, 250 g pack' (35 chars). Wrong: 'Don't miss out! Best chai at Rs 99!!' (exclamation, price, superlative).

Asset-based set, five angles: 'Masala chai with whole cardamom and ginger' (42); 'Assam tea blended in small batches in Pune' (42); 'A kadak cup of chai, made at home' (33); 'Chai for gifting, packed in Pune' (32); 'Cardamom Kadak: a strong morning blend' (38).

Brand name 'Brew Rani' (9 chars). Body text: 'Small-batch Assam tea with whole cardamom and dry ginger. Packed in Pune and delivered across India.' (100 chars). Disclaimer: 'Image is for illustration only.' (31 chars).
Custom image copy: 'Chai made the kadak way' (5 words). Aim for 4-6 words so the type stays large.
Every headline claim has to be true of the product detail page. If the client cannot prove it, cut it.

cards.name: Amazon Sponsored Brands ad (headline, logo, products)
cards.summary: A Sponsored Brands ad is a search ad with a logo, a custom headline and 3 or more products (Collections), a Store spotlight, or a video of 6 to 45 seconds. Amazon's public pages do not state the headline character cap (the 50 quoted widely is printed officially only for DSP display), but its moderation rules are explicit: sentence case, no more than two repeated ?/! marks or ellipses, and no unproven claims.
use_for: Custom headline for a Collections ad over 3 or more products.
Headline for a Store spotlight ad (the Store needs at least 4 pages).
Planning the words and length of a Sponsored Brands video (6 to 45 s, 20 s or less highly recommended).
Cleaning a headline that Amazon moderation rejected.
avoid: Title Case, ALL CAPS or mixed case. Amazon rejects them; capitalise only the first word, proper nouns and trademarks.
Numerals, *, @ or periods in place of letters, or to shorten words ('H8', 'w/out'), unless part of a brand or slogan. Spell the word out.
'???', '!!!' or long ellipses. The limit is 2 instances per headline.
Claims the product page does not support. A headline claim needs proof and must match the product detail page.
Naming specific products in an optimized ad's headline. Amazon says optimized ads must carry general headlines.
Treating 50 characters as Amazon's Sponsored Brands rule. It is not published for this ad type; draft to 50 as a safe proxy and let the console's live counter decide.

Writing the headline in a language other than the site's primary language. Ads must be in the primary language of the site; confirm in the console whether Hindi is accepted on Amazon.in before writing it.

sources.title: A complete guide to Sponsored Brands and display ads moderation - Amazon Ads
sources.supports: headline punctuation, sentence case, special characters, claims substantiation, optimized-ad headline rule

sources.title: Create a Sponsored Brands campaign - Amazon Ads help
sources.supports: formats: Collections (logo + custom headline + 3 or more products), Brand Gallery, Store spotlight

sources.title: Sponsored Brands video - Ad specs and guidelines
sources.supports: ad anatomy (headline text, logo, CTA), video duration

limits.field: repeated ?/! marks or ellipses per headline
limits.quote: Repeated question (???) or exclamation (!!!) marks or excessive ellipses—generally more than two instances per headline—must not be used.
Video duration Between 6 and 45 seconds (20 secs or less highly recommended)

formatting: Headline: plain text in sentence case only (first word, proper nouns, trademarks capitalised).
No numerals, *, @ or periods used instead of letters or to shorten words (unless part of a brand or slogan, or symbols such as $ and #).
No more than 2 repeated question marks, exclamation marks or ellipses in one headline.
Collections: logo + custom headline + 3 or more products. Store spotlight: needs a Store with at least 4 pages. Video: headline text, logo and CTA; 6 to 45 seconds.
Language: the primary language of the site.
Emoji, bold, line breaks and Devanagari are not covered by the pages read: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: this card has no lintable limit (one count, one duration), so `pcw.py check --platform plat:amazon_sponsored_brands` tests no length. Read the draft against the rules above by eye; count '?', '!' and ellipses by hand (limit 2).

Conflict on the headline cap: no Amazon page read states one for Sponsored Brands; the 50-character figure is official only for DSP creatives (plat:amazon_dsp_display). Draft to 50 or under so the line survives either way, and read the console counter before delivery.

Headline formula: the category or need that all the products share, in sentence case, no specific product. 'Small-batch chai blends from Pune' (33 chars) or 'Chai for slow mornings' (22 chars). Wrong: 'BEST CHAI W/OUT SUGAR!!!' (capitals, a symbol shortening 'without', repeated '!').
Write the headline last: pick the 3 or more products first, then name what they have in common.
Video: plan the whole message to fit 20 seconds; Amazon says 20 s or less is highly recommended and only allows 6 to 45.
Any claim ('no added sugar', 'handmade') needs proof on the pack or product page. If it is not there, the claim is out.

algorithm_notes.note: Amazon moderation: optimized Sponsored Brands ads must contain general headlines that do not mention specific products.

cards.name: Apple Podcasts show and episode (Apple Podcasts Connect)
cards.summary: The four text fields in Apple Podcasts Connect: show name up to 150 characters, show description up to 4,000, episode title up to 150, episode description up to 10,000. A show delivered by an RSS feed from another host follows that host's limits, and the industry feed figure is 4,000 for show and episode notes, so notes written under 4,000 work on both.
use_for: Show name and show description when submitting a new show.
Episode title and episode description for each release.
Hindi, Hinglish or English show notes that must also work on Spotify and other apps.
Rewriting a show description so a new listener knows who it is for.
avoid: Using the 10,000-character episode limit as the target when the show is fed from another host. The host's limit applies; the industry-wide figure is 4,000, so keep episode notes under 4,000 and the same text works everywhere (plat:spotify_podcast_episode).
A show description that lists past episodes. Say who the show is for, what they get, the format and the cadence.
A title that spends its first words on the show name or an episode number. Put the topic first; the limit is 150 but the first words are what a listener scans.
Show notes that only say 'In this episode we talk about...' Name the guest's credential, the question answered and the next step.
Assuming Devanagari counts like Latin characters. The pages read do not say how Apple counts them; leave a margin.

sources.title: Apple Podcasts for Creators: Submit a new show
sources.supports: show name 150, show description 4000

sources.title: Apple Podcasts for Creators: Create an episode
sources.supports: episode title 150, description 10,000, art 3000x3000

You can enter up to 4000 characters.

Description : One or more sentences describing your episode to potential listeners. You can enter up to 10,000 characters.
limits.confidence: high (Apple Podcasts for Creators, Create an episode)

formatting: Fields: Name (show, 150 characters), description (show, 4,000), episode name (150), episode description (10,000), all entered in Apple Podcasts Connect.
Episode art can be 3000 x 3000 pixels (Apple's 'Create an episode' page).
A show delivered by RSS from another host follows that host's field limits, not Apple's.
How links, line breaks, bold or timestamps render in the description is not covered by the two Apple pages read: unverified; test in Connect before delivery.
Hindi and Devanagari counting is unverified: leave at least 10% of the limit free.
writing_notes: Lint: four lintable fields, so pass --field: `--field "show name"` (150), `--field "show description"` (4000), `--field "episode title"` (150), `--field "episode description"` (10000). Paste one field per run.

Conflict: Apple's Connect limits (4,000 / 10,000) versus the industry feed figure (4,000 for both show and episode notes). Trust Apple for shows hosted in Connect and the other host's cap for shows fed by RSS. When unsure, write episode notes under 4,000.

Show description shape: who it is for and what they get, then format and cadence, then the host's credential. 'Har hafte 20 minute mein GST aur income tax ki ek asli problem, ek Jaipur CA ke saath. Chhote business owners aur D2C founders ke liye, Hinglish mein, bina jargon ke. Naya episode har Tuesday.' (192 chars, Hinglish in Roman script).
Show name: the name people will say aloud, not a keyword string. 'Seedha GST' (10 chars). Put the topic words in the first sentence of the description.
Episode title: topic first, then the payoff. 'GST notice aaya hai? Reply likhne se pehle yeh 3 cheezein dekhein' (65 chars).

Episode description: first two sentences carry the topic and the payoff, then guest credential, timestamps, links. 'Ek Jaipur CA batati hain ki GST notice milne par pehle kaunse documents nikalein, portal par notice kahan dikhta hai, aur reply ka format kaise banayein. Timestamps neeche hain.' (177 chars before timestamps).
Hinglish in Roman script suits a Hinglish show; keep one script per field and match the language the audio is in.

cards.name: Behance project (title, tags, description)
cards.summary: A Behance project needs a cover image, a project title and at least 1 creative field before it can publish, and takes up to 10 project tags. Behance publishes no character limit for title or description; its own guidance describes the average project as 10 to 15 images broken up with descriptive text and a compelling title.
use_for: Project title for a portfolio case study.
Short text blocks between images: the brief, the process, the result.
Choosing up to 10 tags (discipline, industry, tools).
Credits and role lines for a team project.
avoid: A generic title such as 'Branding project 3'. The title is one of three required items; name the client or brand and the job in plain words.
One long essay above the images. Behance describes projects as images broken up with descriptive text, so put one short block of text beside each image group.
Ten tags chosen at random. Tags and tools are suggested, not required, so use them for what a hiring manager or client would filter by: discipline, industry, tool.
Showing client work you have no permission to show. Check the client agreement and any NDA before publishing.
Quoting a title or description character cap. None is published; do not invent one.

sources.title: Behance Help: Project Tags
sources.supports: up to 10 project tags

sources.title: Behance Help: What fields are required before publishing?
sources.supports: cover image, project title and at least 1 creative field required

sources.title: Behance Help: Create & Publish A Project
sources.supports: tags and tools suggested, not required; description under Co-owners, Credits, and More

sources.title: Behance Help: Advanced Project Settings

limits.quote: You can add up to 10 Project Tags

formatting: Required to publish: a cover image, a project title and at least 1 creative field.
Project tags: up to 10. Tags and tools are suggested during creation, not required.
The description sits under 'Co-owners, Credits, and More' in the create-and-publish flow; descriptive text also sits between images.
A typical project has 10 to 15 images broken up with descriptive text and a compelling title.
A project can be scheduled up to 90 days ahead.
Bold, links, lists and Hindi or Hinglish text inside text blocks are not covered by the help pages read: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: the only recorded limit is a tag count, and `pcw.py check` cannot count Behance tags (its counter only recognises hashtags, emoji, mentions, links). `check --platform plat:behance_project` therefore tests nothing; count the 10 tags by hand.

Title formula: brand or project name + the job in plain words. 'Brew Rani: packaging and brand identity for a Pune chai brand' (61 chars; no cap is published, so shorter is better for the cover and for sharing).

Text block shape, one per image group: a short heading naming the section (The brief, The idea, The result), then 1-3 sentences, then one number or fact. Example: 'The brief. Brew Rani sold only through marketplace pages and needed a pack that reads as small-batch even as a thumbnail.' Add real figures only if the client has confirmed them.

Ten tags, in this order of priority: 2-3 disciplines, 1-2 industries, 2-3 tools, then style or place. Example: packaging design, brand identity, illustration, tea, FMCG, Pune, Adobe Illustrator, Adobe Photoshop, typography, label design.
End with a credits block: your role, collaborators, tools and year. A hiring manager scanning for what you did personally should find it in one place.
Write in first person plural for a studio, first person singular for a solo piece, and keep the verbs concrete (drew, tested, shipped).

cards.name: Bing search result (title + meta description snippet)
cards.summary: How a page's HTML title and meta description appear in Bing, and what Copilot sees. Bing publishes no title cap and may truncate or rewrite either element; the meta description shows roughly 160 characters according to an official 2012 Bing Webmaster post. Current Bing guidelines say missing, duplicate or overly short titles and descriptions can hurt indexing reliability, ranking and eligibility for grounding and citations.
use_for: Title and meta description pairs for service, product and article pages.
A unique pair for every page of a site that has duplicates.
A meta description written as a call to action for a page that already ranks.
Pages that should be quotable in Copilot answers.
avoid: The same title or description on many pages. Bing says duplicate ones may reduce indexing reliability and ranking.
Very short titles and descriptions. 'Home' or 'Services' are 'overly short' in Bing's words.
Putting the brand first on a long title. Bing needs to fit titles in the available space and may truncate long ones, so lead with the words that matter.
A title that disagrees with the page's heading and content. Bing asks you to align titles with headings and content.
Treating 160 as a hard rule. It is 'roughly 160 or so' from a 2012 official post; write so the answer lands before the cut.

sources.title: Webmaster Guidelines - Bing Webmaster Tools
sources.supports: titles and meta descriptions matter for indexing, ranking and Copilot grounding; align titles with headings and content

sources.title: Does Bing like SEO? You bet your ahrefs we do (Bing Webmaster blog)
sources.supports: meta description as a call to action, ~160 visible characters

sources.title: How Does Bing Choose The Title For My Web Page? (Bing Webmaster blog)
sources.supports: Bing truncates long titles and may rewrite them from OpenGraph, page text or anchor text

limits.field: meta description shown in the result (approximate)
limits.quote: Those roughly 160 or so characters that appear in the SERP are really a chance to sell your site to the searcher.

formatting: Title and description come from the page's HTML title tag and meta description.
Bing may rewrite a title using OpenGraph, page text or anchor text, and may move the site name to the front to keep it from truncating.
Long titles are truncated to fit the space; no character cap is published.
Meta description shows roughly 160 characters in the result (official 2012 post).
The NOCACHE meta setting limits Copilot to the URL, title and snippet.
Emoji and Devanagari display in results are not covered by the pages read: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: one lintable limit, so `pcw.py check desc.txt --platform plat:bing_search_result` tests the META DESCRIPTION against 160. Bing has no title cap; test a title with the Google card's guidance: `pcw.py check title.txt --platform plat:google_search_result --field "title tag"` (60, third-party, a safe proxy).

Conflict: Google and Bing both set no hard limit; the 60 and 160 numbers are guidance. Write the title to 60 or under and the description to 155 or under so it holds in both, and put the key phrase first.
Title formula: the page's subject and primary phrase first, brand last. 'GST notice reply for D2C brands | Sharma & Rao CA' (49 chars, inside the 60 proxy).

Description formula: answer the searcher's question, then one proof or action. 'Got a GST notice? Jaipur CAs read the order, gather the documents and file the reply on the portal. Book a 15-minute call to see your options.' (142 chars). Bing calls it a chance to sell the site: end on a clear next step.
Write a different pair for each page, and make the title agree with the H1.
Missing, duplicate or overly short pairs are what Bing's own guidelines warn about, so audit those before polishing the good ones.

algorithm_notes.note: Bing Webmaster Guidelines: missing, duplicate or overly short title tags and meta descriptions may reduce indexing reliability, ranking and eligibility for grounding results and citations.
Bing truncates long titles and may rewrite them from OpenGraph, page text or anchor text, so the most important words belong at the front.

cards.name: Business Wire news release (BusinessWire.com distribution)
cards.summary: A news release distributed over Business Wire, where the headline becomes the page title tag and the first 160 characters of the body become the meta description in search results. Business Wire's own advice is an 8 to 12 word headline with the primary keyword near the front and the news in the opening lines.
use_for: Headline and opening paragraph of a product launch, funding, appointment or results release.
A release whose search snippet must make sense on its own.
Image captions that double as alt text.
avoid: A headline of 20 words that opens with the company name. Aim for 8 to 12 words with the keyword near the front; the headline is also the title tag.
A dateline or boilerplate that eats the opening. Business Wire's page does not say whether a dateline counts toward the 160, so keep the news inside the first 120 characters of the body.
Writing the headline first. Business Wire suggests drafting it after the body so the key point is in it.
Keyword stuffing. Use the primary keyword in the headline and once in the body.
Images with no captions. Captions become alt text; write them.
Quoting a 250-character headline limit or a 2 to 22 word range. A search summary mentioned both; neither was read on an official Business Wire page.

Emoji and Devanagari handling is not stated: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: two lintable fields, so pass --field: `--field "job title"` (200) or `--field "job description"` (25000). The 100-character minimum is not tested; count it.
The limits are the API schema; the on-site composer may differ. Check the live composer before delivery.
Title formula: role + level, in the words candidates type. 'Senior content writer (B2B SaaS)' (32 chars).

Description shape: 2 lines on what the person will do and why it matters, bulleted responsibilities, must-haves versus nice-to-haves, location and work mode, pay range if the client agrees. HTML-safe example (315 chars):

You will write the product pages, case studies and launch emails for a Bengaluru SaaS company selling to finance teams.

  • Write 4 to 6 pieces a month, from brief to published
  • Interview customers and turn the answers into case studies
  • Work with product managers on release notes
Use plain lists and bold only when posting through an ATS, since other tags are ignored.
Check every line against comp:india_job_ad_non_discrimination.

Conflict: LinkedIn's Recruiter help page says job descriptions are limited to 10,000 characters, while the API schema allows 25,000. Write to 10,000 so the post fits either route (https://www.linkedin.com/help/sales-navigator/answer/1749). (lead fix 2026-10-07)

cards.name: LinkedIn member profile (headline and About)
cards.summary: A member's headline and About. About is capped at 2,600 characters (LinkedIn's Talent Blog) and shows only its opening lines before 'see more', with no official visible-character count. The headline appears in search, under every comment and in invitations; the 220 figure is third-party only, since LinkedIn Help states no number.
use_for: Headline: what you do + for whom + proof.
About: who you help, how, with evidence, and how to reach you.
A ghostwritten profile for a founder or executive.
Rewriting a profile that lists only a job title.
avoid: A headline that is only a job title. It appears under every comment you write; say what you do and for whom.
Using the full 220 characters. Third-party guides say only the first 60 to 70 show in some places (unverified), so put the role and audience first.
An About that opens with 'I am a passionate...'. The opening lines are all most readers see; open with who you help and the result.
Presenting 220 as an official limit. LinkedIn Help states none; check the live counter in the Edit intro window.
Claims you cannot back up. Numbers in an About must be ones the person can confirm.

formatting: Headline: the text below the member's name, shown in search results; edited in the Edit intro window (LinkedIn Help). No limit is stated by LinkedIn; 220 is third-party.
About: an open-ended summary, 2,600 characters at most (LinkedIn Talent Blog). Only its opening lines show before 'see more'; no official visible-character number.
Line breaks, bullets, emoji and Devanagari in About are not covered by the pages read: unverified.
writing_notes: Lint: two lintable fields, so pass --field: `--field headline` (220, low confidence, third-party) or `--field About` (2600, medium). Paste one field per run.
Conflict: no LinkedIn page states a headline limit; the 220 is third-party. Use it as a ceiling, but write the first 60 to 70 characters so they work alone.

Headline formula: what you do + for whom + proof or place. 'Chartered Accountant | GST notices and audits for D2C brands | Jaipur' (69 chars); 'Brand designer for D2C food brands | Packaging, marketplace creative' (68 chars).

About opening: who you help + the result, then the situation you solve. 'I help D2C founders in India reply to a GST notice without losing a week of sales. Most of my clients are founders doing Rs 5-50 crore in revenue who get their first notice and do not know who to call.' (201 chars). Then proof, how you work, and one contact line ('DM me GST').
Write the About in first person for a personal profile. A ghostwriter should take facts and numbers from an interview, never invent them.
English for B2B profiles; use Hindi or Hinglish only when the audience is Hindi-first.
